sections.h2: Which office handles Cass County land records?
sections.html:
In Cass County one elected official, on a four-year term, fills both the Clerk and Register of Deeds roles. Besides land records, that office serves as clerk to the circuit court, the board of commissioners, the plat board and the jury board, as registrar of vital records, and as the county's chief election officer. The same counter handles marriage licenses, concealed pistol permits, assumed business names and notary commissions.

Find the office at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis. The phone is 269-445-4464 and the fax is 269-445-4406. Call to confirm counter hours before you drive in with an original deed.

For occasional users, the county runs a basic deed search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. The index search costs nothing. Looking at, printing or saving an image runs $1 a page plus a processing fee. Staff searches are done as time permits, so allow extra days. Clerks will pull a single document you identify, but they cannot search real property records or draw up a list of recorded instruments for you.

The price of a recording has been $30 since October 1, 2016, however many pages the document runs. Where one paper assigns or discharges several instruments, each additional instrument costs $3. MCL 600.2567 is the state basis. Keep staples away from checks.

  • A treasurer's tax certification, $5, is required for warranty deeds, land contracts and assignments of them, and may be added to the recording check.
  • UCC terminations and fixture filings: $30 each. Financing statements go to the State of Michigan only.
  • Copies: $1 a page, $5 for a plat of record, $5 by fax; certifying a copy is $5.
  • Staff searches: half a dollar for each year covered with a $5 floor, $3 per name for state or federal tax lien certificates, and $6 for a financing statement certificate on one debtor name.

sections.h2: What the Cass County checklist requires of a deed
sections.html:
The county posts twenty requirements. Many echo MCL 565.201, and several are more explicit than the statute itself.

  • The land's complete legal description.
  • A notary block giving the notary's signature, commission expiration date, the county and state of certification, the names of those acknowledging, and where the paper was signed.
  • A notary seal if the notary is out of state.
  • Social Security numbers cut to the last four digits, unless a law or court order calls for more.
  • An affidavit explaining the correction whenever an original is recorded a second time.
  • A recorded death certificate, attached or cited by liber and page, wherever a grantor is described as survivor.
  • The consideration stated on the deed itself. Wording such as "other good and valuable consideration" is accepted only with an affidavit.

Layout follows the statewide rule: a blank 2 1/2 inches above the first line of page one, half an inch on other edges, black print of at least 10 points on white 20-pound paper, and a sheet no smaller than letter or larger than legal.

sections.h2: What a Cass County tax certification covers
sections.html:
MCL 211.135 sets up a two-part certificate. First, the county or state treasurer says whether any tax liens or tax titles are held on the parcel and whether taxes are paid for the five years preceding the instrument's date. Second, the treasurer of the city, village or township where the land lies reports on tax titles and tax sale certificates, and on whether those titles, certificates and sold special assessments were redeemed over the same five years.

Timing can matter. Paper presented from March 1 on, before the local treasurer has filed the year's delinquent return, receives a county treasurer notation that the return could not be checked. That gap is not a reason for the register to turn the deed away.

If a tax certificate or special assessment has been sold against your parcel, redeem it through the village or township and collect written proof ahead of closing, because the statute requires evidence of redemption.

sections.h2: How is transfer tax figured on a Cass County closing?
sections.html:
The same rates apply here as elsewhere in Michigan: 55 cents for the county per MCL 207.504 and $3.75 for the state per MCL 207.525, each applied to every $500 of price or any leftover part of $500, so a price of $218,001 would count as 437 blocks. The typical owner-occupied value in Cass County is $218,000, which divides into 436 blocks.

Cass County transfer tax by sale price
Sale priceCounty (0.55)State (3.75)Combined
$120,000$132.00$900.00$1,032.00
$218,000$239.80$1,635.00$1,874.80
$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

When a deal includes personal property, only the real estate is taxed, as long as the deed or an affidavit states the two values apart.

MCL 207.505 and MCL 207.526 share most of their exemptions. The ones most likely to matter in Cass County are below.

  • Land contracts, while legal title waits for the final payment.
  • Quitclaims that only confirm a title the grantee already holds.
  • Boundary-line deeds with no payment attached.
  • A joint tenancy among people when at least one already owned the land.
  • A husband's or wife's deed that creates or dissolves a tenancy by the entireties.
  • On the state list alone: deeds from a parent or grandparent to a descendant, including step and adopted relations, and a dissolving company's transfer to its owners.

An exempt deed still has to meet every format rule, so ask the Clerk/Register how to word the exemption before you sign.

sections.h2: Which Cass County communities record in Cassopolis?
sections.html: Every parcel in the county records in Cassopolis, whether the house sits in a city, a village or open country. The cities and villages are Dowagiac, Cassopolis, Edwardsburg, Marcellus and Vandalia, and unincorporated places include Adamsville, Calvin Center, Glenwood, Jones, La Grange, Penn, Pokagon, Sumnerville, Union and Wakelee. Library districts give a handy map of the townships: Cass District Library serves Calvin, Howard, Jefferson, LaGrange, Mason, Milton, Newberg, Ontwa, Penn, Pokagon, Porter and Volinia, Dowagiac District Library serves the city of Dowagiac and Wayne Township plus parts of three others, and Marcellus runs its own.

sections.h2: Cass County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Cass County is part of the South Bend-Mishawaka metropolitan area, in the Michiana corner of southwest Michigan. Cassopolis is the county seat and Dowagiac is the largest city.

The county has about 51,677 residents, 26,087 housing units and 21,207 households. Owners occupy 81.6% of homes. The typical owner-occupied value is $218,000, typical gross rent is $916, and half of households earn more than $70,443. Because values run at that level, a typical sale carries a sizable transfer tax bill.

faqs.q: What will a deed cost to record in Cass County?
faqs.a: Thirty dollars per document, whatever its length, plus $3 for each extra instrument on a combined assignment or discharge. A warranty deed also needs the $5 treasurer tax certification, which the county lets you include in the same check as the recording fee.

faqs.q: What is the address of the Cass County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The Clerk/Register office is at 120 North Broadway, Suite 200, Cassopolis, MI 49031. Call 269-445-4464, and do not staple your check to the document.

faqs.q: Is searching Cass County deeds free?
faqs.a: The index is free to search by name, date range, liber and page, document number or parcel number. Viewing, printing or saving a document image costs $1 a page plus a processing fee.

faqs.q: What does the transfer tax come to on a $218,000 sale in Cass County?
faqs.a: The total is $1,874.80, made up of $239.80 for the county and $1,635.00 for the state, using 55 cents and $3.75 per $500.

faqs.q: Do I need a treasurer's certificate to record a Cass County quitclaim?
faqs.a: Generally not. The county asks for one on warranty deeds, land contracts and deeds with a covenant of warranty, and MCL 211.135 excludes conveyances without a warranty covenant.
